catalog.label: Order volume
catalog.definition: Units ordered, last 4 weeks vs baseline weekly mean x 4, as fractional change.
catalog.caption: How much less (or more) this account bought recently than its own normal. A drop alone is weak; a drop with other signals is a pattern.

catalog.label: Order value
catalog.definition: Order value (INR), same windows as order_volume_delta.
catalog.caption: Same idea as volume but in rupees, so a mix shift to cheaper products shows up.

catalog.label: reorder_interval_drift
catalog.definition: For chronic-therapy SKUs only: median days between reorders, last 8 weeks vs baseline. Positive = reordering later.
catalog.caption: Patients on chronic therapy need steady refills. When a pharmacy reorders later than usual, patients may be missing doses or switching brands.

catalog.label: Growth with product gap
catalog.definition: Order volume growth for an account in >=2 therapy areas while a complementary therapy area has near-zero purchase.
catalog.caption: This account is growing fast in related products but does not buy a complementary one. That gap is a sales opportunity.

catalog.label: Fill rate
catalog.definition: sum(qty_filled)/sum(qty_ordered), last 4 weeks. Compared to baseline fill rate.
catalog.caption: Share of what the customer asked for that we actually shipped. Falling fill rate usually means a supply problem on our side, not a demand problem on theirs.

catalog.label: Delivery delay
catalog.definition: Mean (delivered_date - promised_date) in days, last 4 weeks.
catalog.caption: Average lateness against what we promised. Customers feel this before they complain.

catalog.label: Stock cover
catalog.definition: warehouse on_hand / trailing 4-week mean daily dispatch, per SKU.
catalog.caption: How many days of this product the warehouse can still ship. Under about a week it becomes the likely cause of downstream customer problems.

catalog.label: Supplier ETA slips
catalog.definition: Number of times inbound_eta has moved later in the last 28 days.
catalog.caption: Each slip of the supplier's promised arrival date is evidence of a supplier or manufacturing delay.

catalog.label: Complaints
catalog.definition: Count of complaints (kinds: service, delivery, billing) in the last 4 weeks vs baseline. COUNT, not rate: this is what deck slide 7 shows ('Complaints up 47%').
catalog.caption: How many more complaints this account raised than it normally does in four weeks. Note that fewer orders with more complaints means the experience got worse, not just busier.

catalog.label: Response time
catalog.definition: Median (first_response_at - opened_at), last 4 weeks vs baseline.
catalog.caption: How much slower we are answering this account. Slow replies make a supply problem feel like neglect.

catalog.label: Regional SLA breaches
catalog.definition: Open tickets older than SLA per 100 tickets, by region.
catalog.caption: When many accounts in one region get slower at once, the cause is support capacity, not individual customers.

catalog.label: Touchpoints
catalog.definition: Visits+calls+WhatsApp touchpoints per 4 weeks vs baseline.
catalog.caption: How much less we are in touch with this account. Relationships fade quietly before orders fall.

catalog.label: Nephrologist visit gap
catalog.definition: Days since last rep visit to a nephrologist linked to a hospital/clinic account, vs that prescriber's usual cadence.
catalog.caption: Doctors who stop being visited tend to prescribe less over time. This catches the gap early.

catalog.label: Rep coverage
catalog.definition: Active reps / accounts per region vs the portfolio norm.
catalog.caption: Accounts per rep. When a rep leaves, every account they covered starts to drift.

catalog.label: Overdue receivables
catalog.definition: Overdue (>0 days past due) outstanding / trailing 12-week billing.
catalog.caption: How much of what this account owes us is late. Paired with falling orders it suggests the customer is under financial stress.

catalog.label: Batch complaint cluster
catalog.definition: Quality-kind complaints for the same batch_id from >=2 distinct accounts within 21 days.
catalog.caption: Several customers complaining about the same batch is a quality pattern. Strata routes it to the QA head and never acts on it automatically.

catalog.label: Possible adverse-event report
catalog.definition: Complaint text classified as possible adverse-event report (keyword + classifier-lite). Routing flag only, not a medical judgement.
catalog.caption: A complaint that might describe a patient reaction. Strata only makes sure a human on the QA side sees it; it makes no medical decision.

catalog.label: expiry_exposure_value
catalog.definition: INR value of channel stock expiring within 90 days where trailing sell-through implies it will not clear.
catalog.caption: Stock sitting at a customer that will probably expire before it sells. This becomes returns and credit notes unless moved.

catalog.label: feed_freshness_lag
catalog.definition: now - last_ingested_at in multiples of expected_every_minutes.
catalog.caption: How out of date each data source is. A stale feed can fake a customer problem, so Strata pauses judgement until the data is fresh.

catalog.label: duplicate_ratio
catalog.definition: Share of rows in the latest load that duplicate an existing order key.
catalog.caption: Repeated rows can look like a sudden spike in orders. A high value means the data, not the customer, changed.
